Needs a wfi: the program deliberately has none, because a core sleeping when the pulse arrives can never be woken and the test would hang on every seed that missed the timing (see the header of tests/programs/custom/mid_run_reset_test/).
No debug stimulus in this test: the FSM never enters DBG_TAKEN_IF (its state itself is uncovered here). Needs reset injection combined with debug_test-like debug_req_i stimulus.
No interrupt stimulus in this test, and IRQ_TAKEN lasts exactly one cycle, so the pulse would have to land in one cycle of a rare event; measured 0 of 12 seeds.
DECODE is where a running core spends nearly every cycle, so a random pulse lands there every time. Retirable only once the merged database of a real batch contains this test.
FLUSH is entered by exceptions and other PC-setting events; this program takes none (measured 0 of 12 seeds). Needs the pulse timed around an exception, e.g. an illegal-instruction loop.
One cycle per divide iteration against a ~35-cycle divide, so ~1/35 of the pulse opportunities MD_COMP gets; 0 of 12 seeds. More seeds, or several pulses per run, would get it.
MD_COMP is the long state of the divider (the rest of the loop retires in ~2 cycles each), which is why this is the only md_state_q edge that lands. Retirable only from a merged batch.
One cycle per multiply; hit on seed 11 only. The functional ALBH->AHBL edge dominates, so this is a real-but-occasional win of multi-seed running, not of the program's design.
The program does no load/store at all, so the LSU never leaves IDLE (4 of its 5 states uncovered). Needs a misaligned access in flight when the pulse lands.

column8: Deliberately not waived. 3008 assert/deassert pulses of the NMI line produced exactly one DECODE->IRQ_TAKEN commit in the whole run (the FSM's DECODE->IRQ_TAKEN transition records hit_count 1) and line 514 was evaluated twice, true both times. The vendored uvma_interrupt_drv_c cannot place a falling edge on the one cycle the window is open: wait_and_assert_irq_edge() holds every rising edge for two cycles and irq_ack_clear() only drops the line after it samples irq_ack -- which is no DUT signal at all (CVE2's interrupts are level-sensitive and cve2_controller.sv has no acknowledge output: its whole interrupt interface is irq_pending_i/irqs_i/irq_nm_i at :66-72) but the testbench's own probe ctrl_fsm_cs == 4'h7 at tb/uvmt/uvmt_cv32e20_dut_wrap.sv:107, which is high during the very IRQ_TAKEN cycle line 514 is read, so the driver drives the line low on the next edge. The narrowest pulse this agent can build is therefore wider than the bin, and the merged .ucdb of the 32-test --all-custom batch (39 per-test databases in it) agrees: 433 evaluations of line 514, 0 hits on this arm.
